---
title: Docusaurus Portfolio

---

## Project overview

I created this portfolio in Docusaurus to learn the platform and showcase my documentation engineering skills.

The portfolio includes:

* A list of my technical writing skills
* A list of Tools I use to create, maintain, and publish documentation
* Case studies of previous projects I completed


It also features:

* Extensive Markdown content
* Autogenerated landing pages under skills/ and tools/ for ease of navigation
* GitHub Actions that run whenever I push changes to the repository:

  * A documentation QA workflow that uses Python and the `requests` library to call the DeepSeek REST API with custom prompts for quality checks. It reviews Markdown content for issues such as grammar, repetition, punctuation, clarity, and consistency and renders the response from DeepSeek as a table
  * A deployment workflow that builds and republishes the site to GitHub Pages
* React and JSX components:

  * Landing-page cards for skills and tools, generated from front matter metadata
  * A responsive marketing grid component that adapts to mobile, laptop, and desktop layouts. It supports two presentation modes: green-tick lists and definition lists. The content is written in plain Markdown and transformed by the component
* A simple Mermaid diagram

## The challenge

The project gave me an opportunity to:

* Learn Docusaurus, React, and JSX
* Learn how to create and configure GitHub Actions workflows
* Write detailed case studies for a technical portfolio
* Integrate the DeepSeek API into an automated documentation QA process

## My approach

The portfolio was treated as a small docs-as-code project rather than a collection of static pages.

Docusaurus provides the documentation framework, with Markdown and MDX used for content and React components introduced where reusable presentation logic adds value.

GitHub Actions automate both deployment and documentation QA. The QA workflow reviews Markdown files using a Python script that calls the DeepSeek API and generates a report containing issues and suggested improvements.

I also created reusable components for presenting skills, tools, and marketing-style content without requiring complex markup in the source files. Where possible, the authoring experience remains Markdown-first, with front matter and simple list structures supplying the data used by the components.

## Deliverables

* This site: a Docusaurus portfolio published on GitHub Pages.
* A QA report for the current site: [Documentation QA report](pathname:///qa/).
* A link from the portfolio to the GitHub repository used to build and deploy it.

## Outcome

The result is an easily maintained portfolio that demonstrates a modern docs-as-code workflow, reusable documentation components, automated deployment, and integrated quality checks.

## What I would change

* Add Vale for deterministic style and terminology checking.
* Add a glossary implemented as a set of Markdown files containing terms and definitions.
* Use the glossary entries to provide hover tooltips when defined terms appear elsewhere in the documentation.
